title: Paragraph Headings Relocated (Option 2: both headings relocated, at the same level -- cell-5 then cell-5)

illustrates.quote: Changing Paragraph Headings to Cell-5 or Cell-7 Headings. A paragraph heading may provide better navigation for the braille reader when it is separated from the paragraph and changed to a cell-5 or cell-7 heading. (See Sample 4-5: Paragraph Headings Relocated on page 4-20 and Sample 4-6: Paragraph Heading Changed to Cell-5 Heading on page 4-21.)

blocks.features: Small bold banner label with a rolled-scroll icon, above the run-in heading.

Bold red run-in heading in print; relocated onto its own line in THIS option and given the SAME cell-5 level as 'Connection to History' (rule 4.5.6's 'equally important' pattern), not the hierarchical cell-7 pairing of Option 1.

print.notes: Option 2 of 3: both headings are relocated onto their own lines, but BOTH are given the same cell-5 level, stacked directly with no blank line between, treating them as two equally important headings per rule 4.5.6 -- NOT identical to Option 1 (whose second heading is cell-7, a 2-cell-deeper indent). Run A's own uncertainty note claiming Options 1 and 2 are byte-identical is incorrect -- see resolution.
print.printFeatures: Same print source as Option 1: small banner label above a paragraph whose first words are a bold run-in heading.

braille.notes: Line 1 the cell-5 heading 'Connection to History'; line 2 the cell-5 heading 'The tree of life' (ALSO a 4-cell indent -- 2 cells shallower than Option 1's cell-7 treatment of the same text), stacked with no blank line, per 4.5.6; line 3 the paragraph begins at column 1.

uncertain: The Darwin paragraph directly follows the relocated heading(s) with no blank line; Emboss's formatPara still applies its ordinary 2-cell first-line indent rather than starting flush at column 1 as the gold braille does -- see standards-findings.md F-39. Expect a documented mismatch limited to this indent, not a content bug.
resolution: braille.lines agree between runs and were independently re-derived a THIRD time directly from .txt lines 3725-3729, confirming line 2 has exactly 4 leading blank cells -- 2 fewer than Option 1's line 2. This directly REFUTES run A's own `uncertain` entry, which claimed "Option 2's braille lines are, character for character, identical to Option 1's": they are not (Option 1 line 2 has 6 leading blanks/cell-7, Option 2 line 2 has 4/cell-5); run A's own braille.lines data array is correct, only its prose uncertainty note was wrong, and it is dropped here. `level` for "The tree of life" resolved to 2 (cell-5): run A said null, and run B's own file says 3 (cell-7) in its print.blocks.level field while its OWN braille.notes prose says "SAME cell-5 indent" for both headings -- an internal inconsistency in run B, resolved here in favour of the directly-measured braille evidence (4 leading blanks = cell-5 = level 2), not either run's stated `level` value.
